2) The invoicing "waterfall" for true-ups (Section 3 of the Exhibit) is vague. We need explicit steps for how credits are calculated when monthly usage drops across tiers (example math), and whether credits carry forward or are netted against future invoices.

Can you share a redline or example invoice calculation? Sophie (procurement) and James (legal) are cc'd — they prefer tracked changes. We have a rolling deadline for signature on 11/24 and would like to resolve these items this week if possible.

Credits calculated under the Stabilization Buffer will be applied as described in the Invoicing Waterfall (Exhibit F, Section 3).

Team — looping you in with the external comments from Helix (see Sophie). I attached an annotated Exhibit F with inline edits (ExhibitF-annotated.pdf). Key asks and my recommendations: 

1) Definition and scope of Stabilization Buffer (Clause 1.2)
   - Recommend: limit to first 12 months OR first major version bump; Buffer used for smoothing only and cannot be resold/repurposed.
   - Pricing impact: simple cap at 20% cumulative credits per quarter to limit exposure.

2) Invoicing waterfall (Section 3) — propose explicit steps:
   a) Detection window: determine sustained underutilization over 60 consecutive days;
   b) Calculation: compute monthly shortfall relative to committed baseline, apply stabilization buffer to reduce shortfall;
   c) Application: credits applied to next invoice;
   d) Cap: credits in any rolling 12-month period capped at 20% of quarterly billed amount;
   e) Reconciliation: annual true-up resets caps and reconciles net.

3) Example calculations: see billing-waterfall-matrix.xlsx — shows two scenarios (gradual decline, sudden drop + recovery). Pricing to confirm numbers.

Irene — legal: please advise if the 60-day detection window and 20% cap are acceptable from a risk/precedent standpoint. Also comment on language that says credits are "applied to next invoice" vs "offset against future invoices until exhausted" — Helix prefers explicit carry-forward language.

Karthik / Laura — can you run the 3 scenarios and confirm P&L impact (attach a one-page memo)? We should be prepared to offer a one-time ramp (grace ramp) in year 1 to help adoption with lower cap for the first 6 months.

Goal: respond to Helix by COB Wed 11/17 with tracked edits and an example invoice.

Attachments: ExhibitF-annotated.pdf (annotated), billing-waterfall-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

-Mateo

Thanks Mateo — see attached redlines. High-level points from Helix legal: 

- Definition scope: Helix is OK with a 12-month limit but insists the Buffer be explicitly reflected both in the Exhibits and Schedule A pricing table so our finance ops can reconcile.

- Credits vs offsets: We want credits to be carried forward as an invoice offset until exhausted; we do not want unilateral vendor discretion to treat them as "one-off" credits. Please revise language from "applied to next invoice" to "applied to subsequent invoices until exhausted, subject to the cap below".

- Cap mechanics: We propose a higher cap (30% per quarter) rather than 20%, but accept a 12-month aggregate cap. We need example math with a sample 6-month decline followed by recovery.

- Auditability: All calculations must be accompanied by a CSV export of the monthly usage and the calculation steps; also request a 10-business-day review window on sample calculations.

We attached Helix_redlines_11_15.docx (redline and comments). We'd like to see your tracked changes by 11/17 to keep signature on track for 11/24.

Sophie / James — thanks for the quick review and the redlines. We've incorporated Helix's preference for carry-forward offsets and adjusted the cap mechanics in the revised amendment. Below is the agreed proposal for the contractual text (draft language):

--- DRAFT CLAUSE (Exhibit F, Section 3) ---

"Stabilization Buffer": means a monthly usage allowance, equal to 15% of the baseline committed units for the applicable month, applicable for twelve (12) months following the Effective Date (the "Buffer Period"). The Buffer shall be used solely to determine invoicing smoothing per the Invoicing Waterfall and shall not be transferrable.

Invoicing Waterfall: On determination of sustained underutilization (i.e., at least sixty (60) consecutive days with usage below the committed baseline), Redwood will: (a) calculate the monthly shortfall net of the Stabilization Buffer; (b) generate a calculation CSV that shows the shortfall, the application of the Buffer, and the resulting credit; (c) apply credits as offsets to subsequent invoices until exhausted; provided that the total credits applied in any rolling twelve (12) month period shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the aggregate billed amount for such rolling period.

Example (attached InvoiceExample-Calc.csv):
- Baseline: 1,000 units / mo
- Month 1 actual: 800 -> shortfall 200; Buffer (15% of baseline) = 150 -> net shortfall = 50 -> credit applied to next invoice = $X
- Months 2-6: see attached CSV for cumulative carry-forward and cap math.

We have attached: ExhibitF-Amend-v2.pdf (tracked edits), InvoiceExample-Calc.csv (worked example), and updated billing-waterfall-matrix.xlsx in the shared Drive. If this matches Helix's expectations, we will prepare the MSA/Exhibit for signature and provide the calculation CSV export each month for your 10-business-day review window.

Proposed next steps:
- Sophie / James: confirm the 15% Buffer number and 30% rolling cap (Helix previously suggested 30% but Sophie flagged operational concerns — if you want a different split for year 1 we can do a ramp).
- Irene / Legal: confirm that the language "Buffer shall be used solely to determine invoicing smoothing" is defensible; if not, propose edits.
- Laura / Karthik: finalize the one-page P&L impact (I have requested this separately).

Let's target a 30-min call Thu 11/18 to finalize.
